title: Create, open, and save source maps
summary: Work with editable Radiant .map files and keep source separate from compiled previews.
outcome: You have an editable .map saved at the intended path.

sections.title: Start from a source map

steps.title: Create or open
steps.text: Choose File > New map for an empty document, or File > Open .map… and pick a local Radiant source file.

steps.title: Check the result
steps.text: After opening, the views frame the map. If the status reports unsupported primitives, they remain in the document and are preserved on save but are not displayed for editing.

tips: Opening or creating another map prompts you to save, discard, or cancel when the current document has unsaved changes.

sections.title: Save the editable map

steps.title: Save the document
steps.text: Choose File > Save. On the first save, choose a .map path; use Save As… to write a different path.

steps.title: Resolve a save error
steps.text: Read the Cannot save map dialog, correct the path or map content it identifies, and save again. A failed save does not mark the document as saved.

paragraphs: Build > Open .d3dbsp preview opens a compiled read-only preview; it is not an editable .map import. View > Import leak path (.lin)… overlays a diagnostic leak path and does not add map geometry.
